A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ROADWork and its recognition, observation, analysis and navigation tasks. The text, tables, figures, equations and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on object recognition, work-zone discovery, sign reading, scene descriptions, geographic adaptation and pathway prediction, including additional pathway results in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds experiments on external work zones, newer models, video augmentation, label unification and performance after fine-tuning in Appendices B–C.

M1.justification: v2 introduces SAM2 video label propagation as a training component for coarse and fine-grained segmentation. Its reported reconstruction procedure also changes substantially: v1 describes COLMAP with video-GPS alignment, whereas Appendix B.3 uses Street View anchors, retrieval-based feature matching and GLOMAP, explicitly discarding smartphone GPS during alignment. The YNet prediction architecture and detector-conditioned captioning procedure remain.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluated work-zone subsets covering adverse weather, night, rural dashcam distortion and front/side bus viewpoints (Appendix B.1; Table 13). Previously discovered BDD100K/Mapillary images receive annotations for detection and segmentation evaluation, beyond v1's discovery task. New evaluations also cover common-category detection and COCO-Captions, substantially broadening task and environmental coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding segmentation comparisons add OMG-LLaVA and Mask DINO, and the manual-mask comparison adds SAM2. Sign-reading and description tables add GPT-4o and Gemini 2.5 Flash. Appendix comparisons introduce Grounding DINO, DiffusionDet, DINO, UniDetector and LLaVA-NEXT. The coarse Mask R-CNN copy-paste comparison is removed, although its fine-grained counterpart remains.

E3.justification: New protocols include Boundary-IoU evaluation, unified-label training tested on Cityscapes, and before/after fine-tuning evaluations on common datasets. v2 also tests 13B/34B VLM configurations and specifies video augmentation over 60 frames, retaining every tenth frame. The 2× Glass crop configuration disappears. Newly disclosed base training counts do not establish that the original split changed.

E4.justification: v2 adds distribution-shift tests, forgetting checks for detectors and VLMs, model-size/generation analyses, label-unification analysis, and SAM2/Boundary-IoU checks of manual-mask necessity. Video-propagation comparisons test an additional augmentation strategy. Geographic adaptation, curvature-based pathway analysis and pathway failure examples already existed in v1 and are largely retained or relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for the experiments. Added results retain single-value reporting.

E6.justification: v2 newly reports Mask DINO segmentation AP of 36.4, or 39.0 with propagation, and fine-grained AP of 30.0/32.8 (Tables 2 and 5). Tables 10–18 add extensive detection, generalization, unification and VLM results; Table 8 adds high-curvature angular-error results. Retained overall YNet and original captioning scores are unchanged. Coarse copy-paste and 2× Glass results disappear. Table 21 also omits v1's separate MMI Pittsburgh count row while retaining the previous totals.

T1.justification: The angular-error definition and probabilistic goal/path formulation are retained, with the equation moved to Appendix C.3. No substantive theorem, proof or formal-assumption change appears. Boundary IoU is added as an empirical evaluation metric without new mathematical development.

C1.justification: The central dataset contribution, four-task agenda and claim that work-zone supervision improves weak foundation-model performance remain. v2 adds contribution-level claims about video propagation and preserving common-scene performance after fine-tuning, and updates dataset scope and headline figures. These extend the existing thesis rather than redefine it.

C2.justification: New interpretations address specialization versus generalization, segmentation-boundary quality, label conflicts, limited benefits from larger VLMs, and caption-style alignment after fine-tuning. Appendix B.4 also qualifies work-zone counts through spatial clustering and temporal ambiguity. v1's detailed future-directions discussion is removed; its camera, missing-path and 3D-perception limitations remain in condensed form.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands acquisition provenance, subset counts, manual verification, reconstruction tools and matching parameters, work-zone clustering thresholds, augmentation sampling and implementation sources for new models. Existing LoRA settings and prompts are retained. The project address changes, while v1's explicit Open Data Commons Attribution license disclosure for the authors' images and annotations is removed; this does not establish an actual license change.

R1.justification: New Table 1 systematically positions ROADWork against common, long-tailed and anomaly benchmarks, acknowledging existing work-zone categories while emphasizing richer annotations and task coverage. Appendix A adds discussion of concurrent RoSA work. References expand substantially around newer foundation models, reconstruction, label unification and forgetting, while several earlier metric and future-direction citations disappear.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten. v1's experimental subsections become standalone recognition, observation, analysis and driving sections; related work and much dataset/experimental detail move into expanded appendices. The standalone Discussion section disappears, with selected limitations incorporated into the conclusion. The title and author listing also change.

P2.justification: v2 adds a dataset-comparison table, reconstruction illustrations, external-condition examples, commercial-driving failure examples and numerous experimental tables. Existing displays are also redesigned: Table 3 places SAM/SAM2 side by side, and Table 8 reorganizes angular-error results. Several introductory figures are condensed, while dataset statistics and pathway examples move to the appendices.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important gaps in v1's generalization evidence through annotated external-condition evaluations, stronger comparator coverage, and checks of forgetting, label unification and model scale (Tables 11–18). Expanded reconstruction and acquisition documentation also improves reproducibility. Loss of the license disclosure, some inaccurate numerical summaries, and Table 21's omitted row with unchanged totals are reporting regressions, but the broader controlled evidence provides a substantial net improvement.
